judgments.reason: Zhang Gui remains the subject; uncle Xi supplies office, not a substitute owner. 泰始初 supplies an era-opening context. The conventional 265 label and actual 266 opening do not conflict with an inclusive lower bound of 265; they prevent an exact 265 or 266 event year. A conservative AD 265+ bound is supported without residual conversion conflict at that chosen precision.

Both named officials own the stargazing conversation. Their reference 張涼州 identifies Zhang already in the Liangzhou appointment narrated from 永甯初. This supports no earlier than AD 301. There is no need to pretend 永甯初 explicitly dates s0016 or supplies an upper endpoint.

惠帝 is the acting emperor, Zhang Gui the recipient of the honor. The honor follows the Yongxing victory in a continuous narrative, permitting AD 304+ from that era lower bound. The source does not close the event to AD 304–306 or an imported death year.

Min accession starts the narrative block; Suo Fu addresses Zhang Gui, followed by adoption and 是時 Liu Yao/Qu Tao action and the emperor dispatching Xin Pan. The Taishi passage is explicitly historical content inside Suo Fu’s quoted speech, not a rewind of his speaking event. 帝 in s0131 has Min as antecedent. AD 313+ is supported for each named actor without assigning exact Jianxing 1 dates or importing later death chronology.

conclusion: All eight existing one-sided lower bounds can be retained as supported partial knowledge. No genuine source-owner, conversion-at-bound-precision, or chronology conflict identified for these eight. Removing unresolved flags is acceptable only with the exact bounds, event ownership, and source limitations retained; exact event years and new upper bounds remain unsupported.
